## Parent

#121 — spec: Expected-set entry resolves its skill files

## What to build

An Expected-set entry resolves and exposes every skill file it owns — the root `SKILL.md`, each runtime variant's `SKILL.md`, and each variant that ships an `agent.toml` instead of a `SKILL.md`. A caller can read which files an entry owns and which one failed, without rebuilding the source layout itself. The entry-level resolution status is left in place for existing callers at this stage; the skill-file facts are the new, authoritative surface.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Enumerating a fixture whose entry is fully resolved returns a skill file for the root fallback and one per variant, each carrying its variant, its resolved path, its kind (a skill file vs. an agent definition), and its own resolution status.
- [ ] Skill files are returned in a deterministic order — root fallback first, then variants in the runtime-variant order — asserted at the enumerator's interface.
- [ ] An entry whose source directory is missing reports its owned skill file(s) as missing with a reason that names the expected location.
- [ ] An entry whose source directory exists but whose root `SKILL.md` is absent reports exactly one missing skill file naming the expected file (the #118 state).
- [ ] An entry whose provenance is malformed reports one missing root skill file anchored at the entry's source root; the entry is still returned.
- [ ] A variant that ships `agent.toml` and no `SKILL.md` yields a resolved agent-definition file, not a missing skill file; a variant directory carrying neither yields a missing skill file.
- [ ] All three Skill sources (autopilot, vendor, upstream) resolve through the same model; an upstream entry's list holds just its root skill file.
- [ ] Every existing consumer and suite still passes: the current entry-level resolution values are preserved by this ticket, and the crate's existing tests stay green.

## Blocked by

- None (can start immediately).
